blocking.section: Health checking and outlier detection; Circuit breakers; Failure matrix (Zone lost, black-holed: pooled HTTP/2 connections)
blocking.issue: Part of the earlier L4X-1 is still open. The 2 s detection comes from `HTTP2Config` pings, which only the `net/http` transport has. gRPC Upstreams use the grpc-go client (Tech stack row 'gRPC upstream client | grpc-go v1.84.x'). The document gives them only 'client keepalive' with no interval. grpc-go raises any client keepalive `Time` under 10 s to 10 s, and a default grpc-go server sends GOAWAY `too_many_pings` to clients that ping more often than every 5 minutes. A black-holed pooled gRPC connection therefore hangs until `perTryTimeout`, which is 7.5 s under the proposed defaults. `timeout` is not in the default `retryOn`, so those attempts end as 504 `RZ-UP-003`. Separately, the per-Endpoint cap only leaves slots free when the lost zone holds under half the Endpoints. Each Endpoint's cap is 2 x its share, so a zone with half the Endpoints can hold every slot. That is the common two-zone case: 2 Endpoints, or 3 per zone in 2 zones, where the caps sum to 1,024. Failure scenario: a two-zone gRPC unary Upstream loses one zone at 1,000 attempts per second per Node. With `round-robin`, 500 attempts per second each hold a slot for 7.5 s, so the lost Endpoints reach their 1,024 combined cap in about 2 s. From then on healthy-zone attempts wait in the 256 pending slots and get 503 `RZ-UP-006` on every Node, until ejection at about 7.5 s. Pure HTTP/2 hits the same exhaustion at about 1,500 attempts per second with `round-robin`, or about 3,000 with `least-request`, for the 2 s to 3 s before ejection. The row's claim that 'the per-Endpoint cap keeps a third free' holds only for three equal zones.
blocking.evidence: "gRPC Upstreams use client keepalive, Planned (M3). A closed connection's streams fail as `reset` and retry, so a black-holed pooled connection is found within about 2 s (target), not at `perTryTimeout`."; "An Endpoint holds at most max(8, 2 × its weighted share of `maxConnections`) in-flight attempts (target), so a black-holed third of equal Endpoints holds at most 683 of 1,024 slots (hypothesis)."; "| Zone lost, black-holed: pooled HTTP/2 connections | Load balancing | Pings fail within 2 s (target); ... holding about 667 slots; the per-Endpoint cap keeps a third free (hypothesis) |"; Tech stack: "| gRPC upstream client | grpc-go v1.84.x |"
blocking.fix: Add a failure-matrix row for pooled gRPC connections. Give the grpc-go keepalive floor (10 s) and the server enforcement risk, and add those facts with URLs to scalability-patterns.md. Give the real time to detection and the RZ-UP-003 and RZ-UP-006 exposure, tagged (hypothesis). For gRPC, and for any attempt that has waited past about 1 s (target) with no response headers, eject the Endpoint on its first attempt timeout while other attempts to it are in flight. Or make it suspect and exclude it from selection once it holds more than its share of in-flight attempts that old. Bound the total per zone: attempts older than 1 s with no headers may hold at most 50% of `maxConnections` (target). Beyond that, the Endpoints holding them are excluded, so healthy Endpoints always keep slots. Recompute the slot figures for a two-zone Upstream and state them in the row, tagged (hypothesis).

blocking.section: Health checking and outlier detection; Failure matrix (Zone lost, black-holed: pooled HTTP/2 connections; Endpoint reset)
blocking.issue: New regression from the L4X-1 fix. A fixed 1 s ping timeout that closes the connection turns any Upstream stall longer than about 2 s into resets of every in-flight stream on that connection. Examples are a JVM full-GC pause, CPU starvation, or two TCP retransmission timeouts on a lossy cross-region link. Reset streams of non-idempotent methods are not retried and return 502 `RZ-UP-004`. Every Node pings on the same schedule, so one 2 s GC pause on one Endpoint fails every in-flight POST to it from the whole Cluster at once. The same stall would otherwise have finished inside `perTryTimeout` (7.5 s). The ping timeout has no field and no stated false-positive analysis. OQ-6 asks about 'ping timeouts', but its options name only `connectTimeout` and `tls.handshakeTimeout`.
blocking.evidence: "a pooled connection silent for 1 s gets one, and no answer within 1 s closes it (target)"; "A closed connection's streams fail as `reset` and retry"; "| Endpoint reset | Load balancing | Idempotent methods retry; others get 502 `RZ-UP-004` | Closed for non-idempotent methods |"; OQ-6: "are dial, handshake and ping timeouts fields? ... (d) `Upstream.spec.connectTimeout`, `tls.handshakeTimeout`"
blocking.fix: On a missed ping, stop opening new streams on the connection and mark the Endpoint suspect, so new attempts go elsewhere at once. Reset in-flight streams only for methods that `retryOn` would retry. Let non-idempotent streams run to `perTryTimeout`, which the per-Endpoint cap and the zone bound in L4X-1 now contain. Or raise the close threshold to about 3 missed pings, or 5 s (target). Give the false-positive rate for a 2 s pause as a (hypothesis). Add a ping-timeout field option to OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-6.

blocking.section: Response caching (rule 3); Failure matrix (State Store out of memory; Ruralz Control leader or Raft quorum lost)
blocking.issue: New regression in the L4X-4 fix. Rule 3's bound 'inside the 30% headroom' fails in two cases the document itself describes. First, count-less Nodes (file mode, or Control-mode Nodes restarted during an outage) each add a fixed 1 MiB per second per shard, which does not scale with `maxmemory` or N. 1,000 file-mode Nodes add 10 GiB per 10 s poll, 61% of a 16 GiB shard. On a 4 GiB shard, 123 Nodes exceed the 1.2 GiB headroom. Second, a counted Node's share is divided by N_published. A frozen or lagging count with N_serving / N_published above 15 therefore passes 30% within one poll, for example a scale from 10 to 200 Nodes during a quorum loss. The document itself sizes Clusters at 1,000 Nodes and says quorum loss freezes the count indefinitely. Failure scenario: an autoscaled Cluster grows from 10 to 200 Nodes during a Raft quorum loss. Cache misses at the cap add 40% of `maxmemory` between two `INFO memory` polls. The shard reaches OOM under `noeviction`, Rate Limits fail open, and `ai.token-budget` returns 503 Cell-wide for up to 25 h. Neither the quorum-loss row nor the out-of-memory row states this.
blocking.evidence: "3. Between reads, each Node caps store bytes per shard at 2% of `maxmemory` per 10 s divided by N_published, else 1 MiB per second (target). The Cell adds at most 2% × N_serving / N_published of `maxmemory` per interval: 20% under a 10-fold count lag, 6% of a 16 GiB shard from 100 file-mode Nodes (hypothesis), inside the 30% headroom."; "If the Ruralz Control leader or Raft quorum is lost, the count freezes at N_frozen all outage long while stale replicas still serve new Nodes."; "Without one, as in file mode, it is 200 × N, 200,000 at 1,000 Nodes (hypothesis)"
blocking.fix: Make the count-less fallback proportional and conservative, for example 2% of `maxmemory` per 10 s divided by 1,000 (target), so it follows the shard size. Also stop stores once a Node sees memory grow by more than 10% of `maxmemory` between polls (target). Or poll `INFO memory` every 1 s when above 50% (target). Or cap the ratio the Node trusts by counting Control Stream peers it can see, falling back to the 1,000-Node assumption when Ruralz Control is unreachable. State the largest safe N_serving / N_published ratio and N for count-less Nodes, tagged (hypothesis). Add the cache-store exposure to the quorum-loss and Scale-out rows.

blocking.section: Rate limiting / Per-Node ceiling; Failure matrix (Ruralz Control unreachable, or no Node count yet)
blocking.issue: Part of the earlier L4X-3 is still open. The restarted-Node row still has no fail-open bound and no worked number. Its new clamp, min(`requests`, 10) per window, is unsafe exactly for small limits, such as the document's own free Tier of 10 per 1s. For those limits the clamp equals the full limit per Node, so the fail-open bound is N_countless x limit. Failure scenario: Ruralz Control loses quorum for an hour and a node-pool upgrade restarts all 100 Nodes. None has a count, because pack 8.11 does not persist it. During a State Store failover, or any time a shard's State client breaker is open, `ratelimit-free` admits 100 x 10 = 1,000 requests per second per client address, 100 x the limit. The frozen-count row for the same outage claims 20 x.
blocking.evidence: "A Control-mode Node without a count clamps to min(`requests`, 10) per window instead (target)."; "| Ruralz Control unreachable, or no Node count yet (Control mode) | Derived ceiling | Last count kept in memory; a Node restarted meanwhile has none: full-limit ceiling, fail-open clamp min(`requests`, 10) per window, 200 first-seen calls per second (target), `node_count_unknown` | Open |"; example: "limits:\n      - {requests: 10, window: 1s}"
blocking.fix: Give the row its bound, N_countless x min(`requests`, 10) per window, with the worked number above, tagged (hypothesis). Replace the clamp with a value safe for small limits: for example one token per window per count-less Node, or max(1, `requests` / 100) (target), which admits at most N_countless per window. Or recommend OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 option (c), persisting the count under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` (a pack 8.11 amendment), and use the persisted count, flagged stale, after restart.

non_blocking.suggestion: A quota key has no local shield: every request before exhaustion costs one script. A single Consumer at 200,000 requests per second saturates a 100,000-call shard (hypothesis) and opens its breaker on every Node, which fails co-tenant `ai.token-budget` keys closed. Add a failure-matrix row 'Hot quota key', and consider reserving quota in leased blocks per Node, for example 1% of the remaining quota or 1 s of observed rate (target), so hot keys cost one script per block.

GCRA uses server `TIME`, so after a failover, clock skew between the old and new primary moves every TAT. A new primary δ ahead over-admits about δ x limit / window per key. A new primary δ behind under-admits until it catches up. Add the skew term, tagged (hypothesis), to the ratelimit failover row.

At 1,000 Nodes the per-Node store cap is about 33 KB per second per shard, under one 128 KiB entry every 4 s per Node. State the Cell-wide store throughput this leaves, so operators can judge cache effectiveness at scale.

Falling back to weighted `random` under the balancer budget silently removes `ring-hash` affinity. Say in the Failure matrix that the Response Cache and hash-affinity Upstreams lose locality under `balancer_budget`.
